clue.text: Companion to conspire in king's downfall

explanation.surface: A courtier plots with an ally to bring down the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess problems, a help-mate is one where Black cooperates with White to get Black's own king checkmated, so both sides conspire in the king's downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or spouse is a helpful companion; and the chess problem term names a puzzle in which both sides cooperate to checkmate one king.

clue.text: Why kids resemble parents, however differently they ride

indicators.note: differently indicates that the letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Children look like their parents however differently they cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Traits are passed on genetically from one generation to the next, explaining family likeness.

clue.text: Property speculator, a fish out of water?

explanation.surface: A developer is a predatory fish out of its element.
explanation.definitionFit: A developer who buys land cheaply to exploit it is a predatory dealer; and a predatory fish living on dry ground would be a shark on land.

clue.text: Cheap material has to be sold in some parts

definitions.text: has to be sold in some parts

explanation.surface: Shoddy cloth must be cleared out in certain areas.
explanation.walkthrough: In northern English dialect 'mun' means must, so 'mun go' is 'has to go' in some parts of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycled woollen fibre is low-grade cloth; and the dialect phrase means it must go, be sold off.

clue.text: One who trifles with a sweet after the cat's started it

indicators.note: after puts the sweet behind the cat, which has started the word

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding

explanation.surface: A cat starts eating someone's dessert while they dawdle.
explanation.walkthrough: Trifles looks like the pudding, which suits sweet and fool, but is the verb to mess about.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon or foolish person behaves frivolously.

clue.text: Notices about party's new lines

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the notices go round the party

parts.note: notices in a newspaper are advertisements, ads for short
Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: Advertisements about a political party are announcing its fresh policy wording.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberals were a major British political party, abbreviated Lib.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvised remarks are lines an actor invents on the spot rather than from the script.

clue.text: Islander kept in order

explanation.surface: An island dweller is kept under strict discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Caribbean republic or of Dominica; and a friar of the Order of Preachers founded by St Dominic is kept in a religious order.

clue.text: Part of book put in behind? Exactly

indicators.note: put in means the answer is placed inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the alphabetical list of topics with page numbers is precisely the section placed at the back of a volume

explanation.surface: Is the section of a volume inserted at the back? Precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the question mark, from the end of 'behind' into 'Exactly'; the surface invites a whole-clue reading about the back of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabetical list of subjects with page numbers is a section of a volume.

clue.text: Rare tiffs with sweetheart

parts.note: a spar is a small quarrel, a tiff
the heart of the word sweet is the letter E

explanation.surface: Quarrels with a lover are seldom.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly scattered and scarce things are few and far between.

clue.text: Has one raised capital internally for book?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: internally means the capital goes inside the other letters
raised in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
A1, read as AI, means capital, first-rate

explanation.surface: Does someone have money invested inside for a book?
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' puts AI into HASI to give HAIASI, which 'raised' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Continue without interruption to enter at speed

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going without a pause and charges in fast.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, text set without a break carries straight on; and an actor or player dashing onto a stage or field comes on running.

clue.text: Service vehicles required for communications

parts.note: Mass is a church service
media are vehicles or channels for conveying something

explanation.surface: Army transport is needed to keep the signals unit running.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers, radio and television are the channels of public communication.

clue.text: Old athletes making record money in Greece

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
the obol was a small coin of ancient Greece; oboli is a plural

explanation.surface: Retired sportsmen cash in by cutting a record in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Discus throwers were celebrated competitors in the ancient Greek games, the plural of the Greek word for them.

clue.text: Cross in ancient temple in Greek island

indicators.note: in places the cross inside the temple word

parts.note: a naos is the inner shrine of an ancient Greek temple
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A crucifix stands inside an old shrine on a Greek isle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest of the Cyclades in the Aegean, where Theseus left Ariadne.

clue.text: Like Lord Lundy's greeting

parts.note: Hilaire Belloc's cautionary-verse peer Lord Lundy was too freely moved to tears, and in Scots to greet means to weep, so his greeting was of the weeping kind

explanation.surface: How did a certain lord say hello?
explanation.walkthrough: Greeting looks like saying hello, but in Scots and Northern English to greet is to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping readily describes Belloc's Lord Lundy, whose career was ruined by his crying.

clue.text: Period of time for new thing to get to West End

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
end means the last letter of the word west

explanation.surface: A novelty takes a while to reach London's theatreland.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: Two weeks, a span of fourteen nights.

clue.text: Old lady of Paris joins ambassador to island

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: An elderly Parisian woman marries a diplomat posted to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is not the French city but the Trojan prince; old lady is slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen of Troy, she was the mother of the prince who abducted Helen.

clue.text: Refitted barges in Eastern Pacific area

indicators.note: refitted ships are rebuilt, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Barges are overhauled in the eastern Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern arm of the Pacific between Alaska and Siberia.

clue.text: What psychoanalysis might do for intimate friend

explanation.surface: Could therapy help a close friend?
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the phrase as a verb and noun: therapy may change one's self.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysis might change one's self; and a second self is a very close confidant.

clue.text: Passes round some cuts of meat

explanation.surface: Someone hands around a plate of butcher's cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To go around the edge of something is to skirt it; and skirt is a cut of beef from the flank.

clue.text: Western girl in European capital, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the capital's name is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria

explanation.surface: A girl from the West is in a capital city of Europe, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Western is not a direction but a surname: Squire Western's daughter in Fielding's Tom Jones.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Tom Jones is the squire's daughter, so she is a Western by family name.

clue.text: Awful girl, grasping one

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a dreadful mess and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A dreadful young woman is greedy and clutching.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is the container's result, GONEIRL, rearranged; the clue as a whole also portrays King Lear's greedy, cruel elder daughter, so it reads as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's eldest daughter is a villainous, grasping woman in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Part of Russia the Yankees marched through

explanation.surface: Union troops marched through a region of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1987 it was a Soviet republic; Sherman's Union army marched through the American state in 1864.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caucasus republic was then part of the USSR; and the southern US state was crossed by Sherman's march to the sea.

clue.text: Bear a prince

explanation.surface: Endure a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear is a British children's comic-strip character; Prince Rupert of the Rhine led Royalist cavalry in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The checked-trousered comic-strip animal; and the Royalist cavalry commander, nephew of Charles I.

clue.text: A French cask free on board

parts.note: un is the French for a
a pin is a small cask holding four and a half gallons

explanation.surface: A French barrel is shipped without charge, as in the shipping term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free on board' looks like the shipping term, but on a chess board a piece is freed by releasing a pin.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, releasing a pinned piece liberates it to move.

clue.text: Certainly not in predicament, note

parts.note: a pass is a predicament, as in things coming to a pretty pass
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Surely not stuck in a tight spot, a note says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in' means not fashionable, the opposite of 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old-fashioned is out of date, definitely not trendy.

clue.text: State — for example, it is connected with church

parts.note: the word it, for example, is a pronoun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nation is, for instance, tied to its established church.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a nation but is a verb, to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or announce something formally, as a judge does a verdict.

clue.text: Gold piece described by space traveller

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A gold fragment was mentioned by an astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite's path is the circular course traced by a spacecraft.

clue.text: Permissive conditions good for race

explanation.surface: Lax rules make good conditions for a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing, the going is the condition of the ground, and easy going suits a fast race.
explanation.definitionFit: A relaxed, tolerant person is laid-back; and soft, comfortable ground on a racecourse is described by the going report.

clue.text: Hit tack

explanation.surface: Strike a nail.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash someone is to give them a beating; and in sewing, to fasten with long loose stitches is to tack.

clue.text: City's second half outside left's score

indicators.note: outside means the city's half goes round the other piece
second half takes the back two letters of the word city

parts.note: left means departed, went

explanation.surface: A football team's second-half outside left scores.
explanation.walkthrough: Outside left was a winger's position in old football formations, a misdirection; 'second half' gives TY from City, which goes 'outside' WENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a set of twenty.

clue.text: Saint seen round an ancient capital

explanation.surface: A holy man is spotted touring an old capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Sant Iago is Spanish for Saint James, whose shrine gives the Galician city its name; the name is also borne by Chile's capital, founded in 1541.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint James is called by this Spanish name; and the capital of Chile and old Galician centre both bear it.
